fields.meta_title: Employee Engagement Survey You Can Act On | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an employee engagement survey with anonymous team results, eNPS, driver analysis and manager action plans. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Employee Engagement Survey From Question to Action
fields.hero_description: Describe your teams and what you need to learn. Emergent builds the questions, anonymous team results, driver analysis and manager dashboards, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What an Engagement Survey Needs to Work
fields.features_subheading: An employee engagement survey measures how committed people are to their work and employer, and what drives that number.
fields.feature_1:
Questions grouped by engagement driver

Core items on pride, intent to stay and extra effort come first, then sections on managers, growth, recognition and workload. Add, reword or drop any item by describing it.
fields.feature_2:
Anonymity thresholds you set

Results stay hidden for any group with fewer than five answers, and comments show no names or emails. The rule is stated on the first screen, so people know who sees what.
fields.feature_3:
Engagement index and eNPS per team

Each team gets an engagement index from the core items and an eNPS from one 0-10 question, shown next to the company result and the team's own score from the last cycle.
fields.feature_4:
Driver analysis that ranks what to fix

Every driver is correlated with the engagement index, so HR sees the handful of items that move it most for each team instead of a page of averages across 40 questions.
fields.feature_5:
Team, site and tenure from your HRIS

Department, location, tenure and manager sync from BambooHR, Workday or any HRIS with an API, so results split by team without asking any employee to describe themselves.
fields.feature_6:
Action plans the next survey checks

Managers log the actions they agreed with their team after each cycle. The next survey asks whether each one landed, and the answers appear beside the action they refer to.

fields.usecase_heading: Engagement Surveys to Build This Week
fields.tab_content_1:
A yearly census that ranks what to fix per team

A 40-question survey goes to all 600 employees for two weeks, with reminders only to people who have not answered. Teams with fewer than five answers stay hidden but still count in the totals. Each manager sees their team's index, eNPS and the driver that moves its engagement most, then logs actions.
fields.tab_content_2:
Frontline staff answer on a phone in two minutes

Store and warehouse staff without a company email scan a QR code in the break room and answer 12 questions in English or Spanish. The code tags each response to its site, and results stay hidden from the site manager until that site has five answers.
fields.tab_content_3:
Find the teams a reorg has unsettled

Six weeks after a reorg, affected teams answer a short survey on role clarity, trust in leadership and intent to stay. Scores are compared with each team's last census, and a drop of 10 points or more alerts the HR business partner in Slack.
fields.tab_content_4:
Track eNPS every quarter without survey fatigue

Each quarter, people answer the 0-10 recommend question and one open question on what would raise their score. A live dashboard tracks the company eNPS quarter over quarter and groups comments into themes, so leaders see the pattern across 400 comments without reading each one.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Engagement Survey
fields.howto_description: An engagement survey is only as useful as what managers do with the results, so the steps start with the decisions you want to make and end with the first action plan.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what you will act on
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the decisions the results should inform: attrition in engineering, manager quality, workload after a hiring freeze. Every question should map to one of them. Items nobody acts on make the survey longer and teach people that answering changes nothing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Use four to six core items for engagement itself: pride, intent to stay, recommending the company, and extra effort. Add driver sections for the areas from step one, written as single statements on the same 1-5 agreement scale.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Set the smallest group whose results anyone can see. Five answers is the usual floor: a group with fewer stays hidden, while its answers still count in company totals. Pull team, location and tenure from your HRIS instead of asking people to describe themselves in ways that identify them.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write it out in plain English: who gets it, which questions, the scale, the anonymity rule and the reminder schedule. Emergent builds the survey, the response database and the dashboards, and you change any part of it by prompting.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell people why you are asking, who sees what, and when results come back. Keep the survey open for two weeks, remind only those who have not answered, and show the response rate by department while it runs.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Read the drivers, not the averages
fields.howto_step_6_des: Start with each team's engagement index and eNPS, then the drivers most tied to them. A low item that does not move engagement can wait. A middling one that does is where the first action belongs.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share company and team results within a month, have each manager agree a short list of actions with their team, and log them on the dashboard. The next survey asks whether anything changed, which is what keeps people answering.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build an Employee Engagement Survey From Question to Action', title 'Employee Engagement Survey You Can Act On' and hero ('the questions, anonymous team results, driver analysis and manager dashboards') cover the whole job, not one feature or a sibling topic.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is Gallup Q12, question lists (Culture Amp, DecisionWise), templates (SurveyMonkey) and vendor directories (SHRM, Perceptyx); the page gives ten example items ('I am proud to work here; I plan to be here in two years...'), a template FAQ, a vendor table and a 7-step how-to.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout ('engagement index', 'eNPS', 'weakest driver', 'HR business partner', 'BambooHR, Workday'); table uses the employee variant: 'Pulse and annual surveys, anonymous reporting, and manager dashboards, as code you own'.

openers.evidence: Every body paragraph opens with a full sentence that says what happens, e.g. tab 2 'Store and warehouse staff without a company email scan a QR code in the break room...'; FAQ 'Not exactly.' / 'Yes.' are direct answers, not labels.

craft.evidence: feature_6: heading 'Action plans, and code you keep' glues two unrelated ideas into one block (manager action logs + GitHub export); give the block one idea (e.g. the action-plan loop) and let the why table/feature carry code export. Also 'two or three' recurs four times (feature_4 'the two or three items', feature_6 'two or three actions', step 6 'the two or three drivers', step 7 'two or three actions'): vary or cut, the repetition reads templated.

voice.evidence: Mostly concrete and plain ('the next survey asks if they landed'; 'Items nobody acts on make the survey longer and teach people that answering changes nothing'). P2 accepted-for-writer: howto_description triplet plus summary ('Seven steps take you from the first question to the first action plan') and FAQ 3 'Because commitment drops long before resignations arrive' (unsourced generalization, defect #7 pattern) are worth tightening in the rework.

truth.evidence: (1) faq item 10 '412 of 600 people answer and the engagement index is 72... The eNPS is +18' reuses tab 1's census (412 of 600, weighted index 72.0) but tab 1's teams give a company eNPS of (118x22+84x9-66x6+141x25)/409 = +15.8, and even Legal's 3 hidden answers at +100 cap it at +16.5; +18 cannot follow (defect #10). Use +16. (2) howto_step_3_des 'Pick the smallest group that can see results, usually five' says the opposite of the intent (it is the smallest group whose results anyone can see). (3) The anonymity rule is stated two ways: feature_2 'any group under five people' and tab 1 'Teams under five' (team size) vs tab 2 / FAQ 10 'once five people have answered' and the image 'Legal 3 answered, Hidden, under 5' (responses). State one rule, fewer than five answers, everywhere. Hidden teams' answers do count in the total (118+84+66+141+3 = 412), consistent with FAQ 10; keep it that way.

distinct.evidence: Own territory per the watch-list (commitment and eNPS drivers): census, frontline QR, post-reorg and quarterly eNPS scenes share nothing with /customer-satisfaction's account-tied CSAT/NPS scenes; satisfaction and pulse are handed off by link in FAQ 13 and 15. P2: the cover ('Rate us as a workplace' five-star card + score) mirrors the CSAT sibling's 'five-star rating and a CSAT of 4.6' cover and uses a star question this page never describes; swap to a 1-5 agreement item or the eNPS gauge.

faq.evidence: 15 items, each answered in its first sentence, but two answers read keyword-stuffed: item 12 asks about 'vendors' then forces 'employee engagement survey providers' and 'employee engagement survey companies' into two sentences; item 14 ends 'instead of reworking a static employee survey template or a sample employee engagement survey from a PDF'. Item 15 link reads 'see pulse survey' with no article; rewrite e.g. 'run a pulse survey'. Also item 15 'a short check of five to ten questions each quarter' contradicts tab 4's quarterly check of two questions.

images.evidence: Each tab is one moment that matches its copy: uc-1 412 of 600 = 118+84+66+141+3, Legal 'Hidden, under 5', Support 'Log actions'; uc-2 'Question 3 of 12', English/Spanish, Store 214 '5 answered' unlocked for R. Diaz; uc-3 Platform 81 to 67 = -14 against a 10-point rule, Slack #hr-partners; uc-4 142+118+86+54 = 400, eNPS +18 up from +12 matching the cover '+6 this quarter'. P2: tab 4 copy says 'eNPS trends by team' while uc-4 shows the company score only.
